summary: Adds a new skill file skills/p-review/SKILL.md defining a one-reviewer adversarial review. The conductor establishes artifact, baseline (via git merge-base fallbacks), and intent, dispatches a fresh subagent with a verbatim brief, rules on findings by vetoing only false premises, then presents Concerns, noted-not-recommended, Rejected, and writes Minor findings to minor-findings.md. A --inline flag skips the subagent and the Ruling step.

claims.text: --inline skips subagent dispatch and the Ruling step; conductor reviews directly using the brief.
Baseline resolves via git merge-base HEAD @{u}, falls back to origin/HEAD, then asks the user.
Reviewer must not report issues that compiler, linter, type-checker, or tests would catch.
Ruling rejects only findings on false premises; all other findings are kept.
Minor findings are written verbatim to minor-findings.md beside the artifact or at repo root, never printed.
Description claims this is cheaper than debate-review, adversarial-review, adversarial-review-2, which exist as skills.

risks.note: Baseline procedure covers only diffs; plans get n/a but conductor steps do not say so explicitly.
Writing minor-findings.md at repo root may overwrite an existing file; no collision guidance.
Asserts craft-vs-fit review is weaker without evidence; stylistic, low stakes.

least_confident: I cannot verify that the referenced sibling skills (debate-review, adversarial-review, adversarial-review-2) exist or that git symbolic-ref fallback behaves as described.
